posts.text: “You cannot build peace on a burning planet,” the UN secretary-general, António Guterres, has warned in a final speech. The outgoing diplomat, and outspoken climate activist, celebrated the progress made in his last decade doing the job while warning of the wide gap between what science demands and politics deliver.…

UN secretary-general António Guterres is now starting his final speech at a Cop in his current function, opening with the importance of facts and truth. “My responsibility has never been to make the facts more convenient.”

A culinary-themed protest has stirred up interest at Cop with activists donning chefs hats to (using a connection that wasn’t immediately apparent) call for debt cancellation for the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries. The protesters from ActionAid, some clutching wooden spoons, said they were serving up a…

Guterres wraps up: “We face lobbies, we face powers, that are pushing pressure on governments. Civil society must put the counterpressure so governments understand that things must change and so we win the battle against climate change.” The session comes to an end with chants in the room of “make the polluters pay”.

Guterres has said the voice of civil society is more important than ever, but told those in the room that the praise he has received is not justified. “I just did my duty. I just did what I was supposed to do. And the duty of the secretary-general is to tell the truth. The duty of the secretary-general is to fight for…
